basics.name: Anang Sahroni
basics.label: Data analysis & scientific software development
basics.summary: Data analyst and software developer with a background in physics and geophysics. From 2020 to 2024 I built real-time data pipelines, REST back-ends and dashboards for sensor data from seismic and magnetic instruments; since 2024 I have been analysing laboratory measurement data at LMU Munich.

work.name: Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
work.summary: Quantitative analysis of laboratory measurement data in paleomagnetism. Funded by DFG (Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft).
highlights: Analysing and quality-checking laboratory magnetometer data with PCA and directional statistics (Fisher distribution) in MATLAB
Planning and running international field campaigns for data collection in six countries (Europe, Africa, Indonesia)
Presenting results internationally: 2 peer-reviewed journal articles, 2 international conference contributions

work.name: Geoseismal Research Center
work.summary: Scientific software for magnetic, gravity and seismic measurement data, from back-end to front-end.
highlights: Technical lead of TARSIUS: designed the real-time pipeline from seismic stations to earthquake parameters (Python, Redis, PostgreSQL)
Built back-ends and REST APIs (Python, Django REST Framework, PostgreSQL) for processing and managing magnetic, gravity and seismic measurement data
Built web front-ends and dashboards (ReactJS) for data processing tools

work.name: Universitas Gadjah Mada
work.summary: Earthquake statistics, seismic hazard and teaching material in Python.
highlights: Built a dashboard of earthquake statistics for Indonesia's provinces (Python, HoloViz Panel)
Probabilistic seismic hazard modeling (PSHA) with OpenQuake
Created Python/Jupyter course material for seismic data analysis: accelerogram processing, earthquake catalogs and location with ObsPy

work.name: Ministry of Agrarian Affairs and Spatial Planning/National Land Agency, Indonesia
work.summary: Hazard mapping for spatial planning in disaster-prone regions.
highlights: Spatial statistical modeling (weights of evidence) of natural hazards around the Palu Special Economic Zone, Sulawesi (ArcGIS, QGIS)

courses: Geomagnetic field behavior and geodynamo characterization at the end of the Cretaceous Normal Superchron
Crustal seismic anisotropy of Sumatra inferred from harmonic decomposition of receiver function.
Determination of the suitable platform and sensor installation procedure on passive seismic acquisition in desert environment using probabilistic power spectral density (PPSD) analysis.
